strings.name: Viola Davis
strings.role: Actor and producer · Stage, film and television
strings.summary: Viola Davis grew up in Rhode Island and trained in theatre, building her career through August Wilson’s plays. She brought detailed physical and emotional work to Doubt, The Help, Fences and the television series How to Get Away with Murder, bringing complex Black women’s experiences to wide audiences. She also produces with her husband Julius Tennon and has used a memoir and its audiobook to consider poverty, trauma and self-understanding.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to films and career honors in 2025. A 2026 interview was checked for recent context; casting and production announcements for later films or series are not presented as finished works.
strings.influence.rationale: Portrayed Black women's experiences in stage and screen works including Fences and expanded opportunities for Black performers in mainstream productions.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-01.value: St. Matthews, South Carolina, United States
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Theatre degree, Rhode Island College; later trained in acting at Juilliard
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Bringing a stage character to the screen
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Played Rose first on Broadway and then in the film Fences, earning a Tony and an Oscar for the respective performances.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Recognition across media
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Her stage, television and film work and the Finding Me audiobook earned Tony, Emmy, Oscar and Grammy awards.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Receives career honors in film and television
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Received the Golden Globes’ Cecil B. DeMille Award and entered the Television Academy Hall of Fame, recognizing her work across media.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Stars in and produces G20
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Played the US president at a summit under attack in an action thriller, producing the film with long-term collaborators.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Finding Me audiobook wins a Grammy
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Won Best Audio Book, Narration and Storytelling Recording for narrating her memoir, completing the Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony set.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Stars in and produces The Woman King
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Worked with Gina Prince-Bythewood as a military leader in a historical action film, expanding her work in women-centered action roles.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Wins an Oscar for the film Fences
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Reprised Rose in the 2016 film, winning Supporting Actress for a performance tracing family relationships and emotional change.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Wins an Emmy for How to Get Away with Murder
strings.timeline.event-06.text: As lawyer Annalise Keating, became the first Black woman to win the Emmy for lead actress in a drama series.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Stars in The Help
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Played domestic worker Aibileen Clark, bringing labor, family feeling and silenced experience into a story about race and social position.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Wins a Tony for the stage production of Fences
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Played Rose opposite Denzel Washington in the revival, winning Best Actress in a Play.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Expands her film profile through Doubt
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Received an Oscar nomination for a brief but emotionally complex mother role, marking an important step from stage work into film.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Wins her first Tony for King Hedley II
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Won Featured Actress in a Play for Tonya in August Wilson’s drama.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Makes her Broadway debut
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Played Vera in Wilson’s Seven Guitars, earning her first Tony nomination and building a stage reputation.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Completes her studies at Rhode Island College
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Completed theatre studies, later training at Juilliard in New York and developing a professional career through regional theatre.
strings.timeline.event-13.title: Born in South Carolina
strings.timeline.event-13.text: Born in St. Matthews and moved with her family to Central Falls, Rhode Island, as an infant, growing up in poverty.
